newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia lending rate drops to 7.8 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatia lending rate drops to 7.8 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate dropped 170 basis points to 7.8 percent on Tuesday as banks sought mostly cheaper short-term loans amid good supply.
The day's trade totalling 46.3 million kuna was overshot by 120 million in supply. Call money accounted for three quarters of all deals.
The weighted call money rate eased 20 basis points to 7.0 percent and banks trimmed their short-term rates slightly.
They granted two-week funds at 9-11 percent, one-month at 13 and two-month money at 10 percent.
The central bank's kuna mid-rate for Wednesday was stronger against the dollar at 6.5558 versus 7.0556 previously, while easing slightly to 3.5703 against the mark.
